author: thebenkogan
body:
The pin checker works by removing the piece from the board, then calculating the legal moves for the opponent in that new position, and then checking if our king is attacked by those enemy moves. If a piece is found to be pinned, it will return no legal moves. 

The only way to order these functions and use a pin checker is if it is passed in as a parameter. I made it an optional argument to legal_moves, with the default being a pin checker that always returns false. This default case is useful when determining the legal moves for the opponent when the piece is removed because we can be attacked by a piece that is pinned, therefore every enemy piece can be viewed as not pinned.

I also moved king_moved, A_rook_moved, and H_rook_moved out to state so that we can have a castling detection function that takes those in and sets a flag in Game.properties (kingside_castle and queenside_castle).

King_in_check will be used later to add an additional filter to legal moves for blocking checks.

body: Resolves: https://github.com/musescore/MuseScore/issues/9379 This PR uses the accidental width to calculate the spacing of key signatures. Before, all accidentals were spaced 1 space apart, regardless of font or symbol. Now, the key signature calculates each symbol's width to space them out appropriately, and the gap between them is `accidentalDistance`, the same style value used for accidentals on chords. This will provide greater consistency and clarity for accidentals. Notes - This PR may not work for custom key signatures. As of today, it looks like it's not possible to create custom key signatures in v4, so I was not able to test it. - Unlike for chords, there does not seem to be much space remove extra space with symbol cutouts. This is because key signatures have well defined patterns (like they move in 4ths or 5ths), and there's just not the vertical clearance in any of the fonts. _The only_ places I could see making the case for adding this is sharps in Peteluma or naturals cancelling out the sharps. If this is desired, I can add that in (though it would increase the scope of the PR quite a bit).

author: ianjhphillips
body:
## Description
Closes #76 
Adds 'Site Admin' role and 'League Admin' roles. 
Implements logic for updating users based on user role.
Adds helper methods for retrieving a user's roles or checking if a role exists.
Adds league_id attribute to User_Role pivot table to track with league a 'League Admin' role pertains to

## How to test
Run `php artisan migrate:fresh`
Open tinker
`php artisan tinker`

Create three users
`$defaultUser = User::factory()->create();`
`$leagueAdmin = User::factory()->create();`
`$siteAdmin = User::factory()->create();`

Create a league admin role
`$leagueRole = Role::create(['name' => "test league admin", 'type' => Role::LEAGUE_ADMIN]);`

Create a site admin role
`$siteRole = Role::create(['name' => "test site admin", 'type' => Role::SITE_ADMIN]);`

Create a league
`$testLeague = League::factory()->create();`

Attach the roles to users
`$leagueAdmin->roles()->attach($leagueRole, ['league_id' => $testLeague->id]);`
`$siteAdmin->roles()->attach($siteRole);`

Run the following commands to test the UserUpdateRequest authentication logic:
`auth()->loginUsingId($siteAdmin->id);`
`app()->call('UserController@update', ['user' => $defaultUser]);`
This should succeed as site admins are authorized to update other users

`auth()->loginUsingId($leagueAdmin->id);`
`app()->call('UserController@update', ['user' => $defaultUser]);`
This should fail.

`auth()->loginUsingId($defaultUser->id);`
`app()->call('UserController@update', ['user' => $defaultUser]);`
This should succeed as the user is updating themselves.

On the user you attached the league admin role to, run:
`$leagueAdmin->isLeagueAdmin($testLeague->id);`
This should return true

`$siteAdmin->isLeagueAdmin($testLeague->id);`
This should return false

`$defaultUser->isLeagueAdmin($testLeague->id);`
This should return false

`$siteAdmin->isSiteAdmin($testLeague->id);`
This should return true

author: ershockley
body:
## What does the code in this PR do / what does it improve?
Previously we always assumed that any data we would want to download was on a specific RSE (UC_OSG_USERDISK), while that obviously will not always be the case. This update aims to select the best RSE based on where the host where straxen is running. 

## Can you briefly describe how it works?
This update uses the hostname (via `socket.getfqdn()`) along with specific environment variables associated with OSG jobs to determine where the code is running, and then determines if the data in question is on a preferred RSE for that location. 

## Can you give a minimal working example (or illustrate with a figure)?
I tested [this code snippet](https://gist.github.com/ershockley/19d38769bb4fd9b3aa425f2cfcf71dfd) on both Midway and Expanse (in development container). It looks for a run on SDSC_USERDISK (which I happen to know are all on UC_OSG_USERDISK at this time also) and then load 2 seconds of raw_records. Depending on which site I run on, the data is downloaded from different endpoints: 

On Midway:
```
Singularity> hostname -f; python test_remote.py
dali-login1.rcc.local
Downloading xnt_018159:raw_records-rfzvpzj4mf-metadata.json from UC_OSG_USERDISK
Loading raw_records: |                                                                            | 0.00 % [00:00<?]Downloading xnt_018159:raw_records-rfzvpzj4mf-000000 from UC_OSG_USERDISK
Loading raw_records: |▏                                                | 0.35 % [00:06<29:05], #1 (6.05 s). 7.5 MB/s
```

On Expanse:

```
Singularity> hostname -f; python test_remote.py
login02.expanse.sdsc.edu
Downloading xnt_018159:raw_records-rfzvpzj4mf-metadata.json from SDSC_USERDISK
Loading raw_records: |                                                                            | 0.00 % [00:00<?]Downloading xnt_018159:raw_records-rfzvpzj4mf-000000 from SDSC_USERDISK
Loading raw_records: |▏                                                | 0.35 % [00:04<22:00], #1 (4.58 s). 9.9 MB/s
```

You can see that when running on Midway, it grabs the data from UC_OSG_USERDISK, whereas on Expanse it grabs it from SDSC_USERDISK.

WooCommerce allows guest checkout (purchase without creating an account or logging in) globally based on a plugin setting, but we can use a `pre_option_woocommerce_enable_guest_checkout` filter to always require a customer account to be created or logged in when purchasing one of the listing products, regardless of this plugin setting. Once logged in after purchasing (or just by logging in via WooCommerce's My Account page), customers can view the listings they've purchased via the Orders tab, or the details of their subscription(s) via the Subscriptions tab. Since they don't have access to the WP admin dashboard, all functionality to manage posts must happen in the My Account UI. ~On hold until #124 and #128 are merged.~ Merged! Closes #37. ### How to test the changes in this Pull Request: This is a fairly big PR that encompasses quite a lot of closely-related functionality. I'll split the testing steps into short phases organized by user story.
User Story: As a site admin, I want to enable self-serve listings and set relevant site-wide options. 1. Features in this branch are gated behind an environment variable in this early stage of release. The features also require the WooCommerce and WooCommerce Subscriptions plugins. As a control, do some light functional testing to ensure that the plugin's features don't behave any differently from `master` when the variable isn't set and/or the required plugins aren't active. 2. Add `define( 'NEWSPACK_LISTINGS_SELF_SERVE_ENABLED', true );` to your wp-config.php and activate WooCommerce and WooCommerce Subscriptions. 3. Go to **Listings > Settings** and confirm there's now a new "Self-Serve Listings" section of options here. 4. Update some of the settings and confirm the settings are saved as expected. - This functionality was already tested and merged as part of #117, but you could confirm that updating prices in plugin settings also updates the pricing of the corresponding WooCommerce products (this is currently one-way only, so updating the prices in WC won't update the values here). 5. Run `wp cron event list` at CLI to confirm that the following cron events are scheduled once daily: - `newspack_listings_expiration_checker` – This job queries published featured listings whose feature expiration date has passed, and unfeatures them. This job was previously tested and merged as part of #128. - `newspack_expire_listings` – This job queries published single-purchase listings whose publish date is more than the number of days set as the "Single listing expiration period" option, and unpublishes them. - `newspack_expire_listings_with_date` – This job queries published listings whose manual expiration date (set as post meta) has passed, and unpublishes them.
User Story: As a site admin, I want to view/manage the WooCommerce products driving self-serve listings purchases. 1. Go to **Products** and verify that there's a set of listings-related products grouped as child products under a parent product. This was previously tested and merged as part of #117. 2. Note that it's technically possible for advanced WooCommerce users to manage these products manually here, but the Newspack Listings feature set was designed to require minimal interaction with WooCommerce.
User Story: As a site reader, I want to purchase a single listing with the most basic options. 1. On a post or page, add a **Listings: Self-Serve Form** block to the content. This was previously tested and merged as part of #128. 2. In a new browser or incognito window (or as a non-logged-in user), visit the post or page with the self-serve block. 3. Make sure the "Single Listing" tab is active, then fill out the form and click "Next." Leave the "Upgrade to a featured listing" option unchecked for now. 4. Confirm that you're redirected to the WooCommerce checkout page with the relevant products pre-selected, and your form inputs reflected under the new "Listing Details" section. Note that if you left the title field blank, the purchase will still be processed, but the listing will be generated with an "Untitled Listing" title. Note also that the "Listing Type" selection currently only determines which block pattern (if any) the post is generated with. We don't currently have any patterns for Job Listings or Obits, 5. Confirm that the pricing of products matches the plugin settings. 6. Confirm that the "Returning customer? Click here to login" prompt is always available, even if guest checkout is enabled or account creation is disabled under **WooCommerce > Settings > Accounts & Privacy**. 7. Fill out the checkout form and payment info, and complete the purchase. (Note: you must have at least one testable payment method active in WooCommerce settings, such as Stripe with test transactions enabled. Check payment is the easiest testable payment method.) 8. On the order confirmation screen, confirm that there are special links to edit your purchased listing and manage your account. 9. author: github-learning-lab[bot]
body:
# Using `request changes` on a pull request Thanks again for all your help on that last pull request. With our powers combined, _anything_ is possible! This next change might introduce some new changes that aren't going to look great. Sometimes, the author might identify that something isn't working. They might need a helping hand :wave: to solve the problem. In other instances, it might only work in their environment. When reviewing a pull request, look at and test the code to pinpoint any bugs or unexpected behavior. ### Writing a review #### Review the `diff` Reviewing the `diff`, the comparison of the proposed code, in the context of the whole project. Could it introduce performance problems, or security vulnerabilities? Try to predict unintended consequences that this change could cause. #### Try it out For most things, actually trying out the proposed change is a good idea. This makes it a lot easier to tell if the actual change matches the intention. You can do this by: - Cloning the repository, and checking out to the branch compared in the pull request. Run the application in your local development environment. - Deploying the pull request to a review-lab or staging environment (as appropriate). When summarizing your review, let the author know if you completed any of these tests. #### Empathy and Constructive Feedback The goal of providing feedback on a pull request is to ensure that the best possible change is being added. Sometimes, a change isn't addressing the problem in the best possible way. It's the reviewer's responsibility to provide meaningful and constructive feedback. ### Requesting Changes 101 Before you submit your review, your line comments are pending and only visible to you. You can edit pending comments anytime before you submit your review. To cancel a pending review and its pending comments, scroll down to the end of the page in the Conversation tab. Then click **Cancel review**. ## Step 4: Leave a review that asks for changes If you could check out this code for me and tell me what is wrong, that would be fantastic. ### :keyboard: Activity: Requesting changes 1. On the pull request, click **Files changed** 1. Hover over the line of code where you'd like to add a comment, and click the blue comment icon 1. In the comment window, type your comment 1. Click **Start a review** - If you have already started a review, you can click **Add review comment** 1. Above the changed code, click **Review changes** 1. Type a comment summarizing your feedback on the proposed changes - _Note: The problem here is that too many Tetris pieces are the same color. In your review, you might want to suggest that I choose colors which would be easier to see when playing the game._ 1. Select **Request changes** to submit feedback introducing changes necessary before merging 1. Click **Submit review**

Return to this pull request for my next comment

> _Sometimes I respond too fast for the page to update! If you perform an expected action and don't see a response, wait a few seconds and refresh the page for your next steps._

author: dl9sau
body:
sprintf("%f", ... rounds up.
In the special case of minute of position > 59.9990 the result is 60.0.
This results in a wrong APRS position location (i.e. 53.60.00N).

This patch also makes create_dao_aprs() nicer and fixes "TODO: optimize ugly float to char to string to int conversion?".

I tested the patch, and the author of the dao_aprs extension, dj1an, has confirmed everythin is still ok.

author: protryon
body:
This PR changes the point for which to scan for forks for reversion to the latest received block in a prospective fork, as opposed to the parent hash.

This prevents us from reverting and ending up on the same chain that we are on in fresh-fork scenarios off old canon blocks.

This also indicates some nodes that should be syncing are mining -- which is likely due to the race condition present in node status.
